title: NY State Senate · District 23
area: Most of the North and East Shores of Staten Island, plus parts of southern Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Jessica Scarcella-Spanton defeated Omar Mohamad in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 72.8% to 26.8% (6,603 to 2,429 votes).
Ruslan Shamal advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party lines without a primary contest.

priorities.text: Has pushed for Staten Island to be included in citywide pre-K ("2-K") expansion, arguing the borough's children were being excluded from a program other boroughs received.
priorities.quote: While the rest of the city revels in the prospects of this program, Staten Island's children are left without any opportunity or equitable access to be part of it. That is a disservice to every child and every hardworking parent in our borough.

priorities.text: Has made veterans' issues a focus of her legislative work, including sponsoring a registry for service members and veterans who may have been exposed to hazardous substances at military installations.

record.text: Sponsored S10515, the "Wireless Security Enforcement (WiSE) Act," which would make manufacturing, importing, or selling wireless signal jammers a class D felony; in the Senate Internet and Technology Committee as of May 15, 2026, not yet passed by either chamber.

Sponsored S10151-A, which would direct the state veterans' services commissioner to establish a registry of service members, veterans, and family members who may have experienced hazardous substance exposure at military installations; amended and recommitted to the Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee on June 1, 2026.
Chairs the Senate Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee.

candidates.name: Ruslan Shamal

priorities.text: Frames his campaign around opposition to democratic socialism in New York City and his personal experience under authoritarian government in Belarus.
Says he would support the NYPD and public-safety initiatives, and would vote to repeal or reform the state's bail laws.
Says he would oppose new taxes and "hidden fees."

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says his Senate votes would support the NYPD with resources and recruitment.
positions.quote: Support the NYPD with resources, recruitment, and respect

positions.summary: Campaign homepage lists backing school choice among his education positions.
positions.quote: Support parents and education policies that work by restoring parental involvement, backing school choice, and keeping politics out of the classroom.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page calls policies like City of Yes top-down mandates that override neighborhood input and increase density without infrastructure, and lists preserving local decision-making and protecting one- and two-family homes among his votes.
positions.quote: Opposing City of Yes style mandates that ignore local input

statements.quote: Stop tax hikes and hidden fees that drive up the cost of living
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, under "How I will vote in Albany"

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site shamalforny.com (checked 2026-10-19) lists positions on affordability, zoning, public safety and education; no statements found on abortion, guns, immigration or other listed issues. Branch.vote profile paraphrases were not used.
